reviews.comment: Dr. Wright is a good person and ECEN451 is a good class. The lectures are alright, and the exams are tough. There are up to 2 projects where you build antennas. The second project was optional and involved beamforming using an array. It was, by far, the most fun, stressful, and informative part of the class and I recommend opting into it.

Lectures are worthless, need to buy and learn from the book to know the content well enough for the exams, which are extremely difficult if you don't read from the book (but relatively easy otherwise). Best part of this class are the projects, where you actually design and build a few antennas. HW's are all over the place, mostly completion grades.

Prof. Wright was...something. Lectures weren't all that interesting. First half of the semester is alright; exams were okay, homework was a little difficult. The best part is the projects, where you build your own antennas. I recommend Wright simply for the experience you get from the projects. Other than that, just study a lot and you're fine.

First, antenna engineering is not a very intuitive topic and can be difficult itself. Dr. Wright's lectures can be boring but that's just cause everything is already on a PDF file to make it easier. Homeworks can be either easy or pretty hard. Tests can be hard. I recommend you take this class and prof if you really want to learn this material.
